      "risks": "Small eigenvalues may mostly represent noise, causing whitening to amplify unstable directions despite shrinkage; global covariance may erase useful broad semantic structure; and any Stage 3 gain may be within seed variance.       "idea_id": "residual_norm_tempering",
      "title": "Temper residual magnitudes across quantization stages",
      "motivation": "In residual quantization, early-stage residuals can be much larger than later residuals, so reconstruction-driven training may over-optimize coarse semantic directions while fine code digits encode little useful distinction.       "novelty": "This changes the scale of the residual presented to each successive quantizer using a deterministic scalar schedule, rather than changing geometry, branching, assignment balancing, or adding a behavior-derived objective. It keeps the same codebooks, number of stages, and global item-to-tuple assignment.",
      "key_change": "Normalize the residual entering each later stage by a fixed stage-specific scalar, while accumulating the correspondingly rescaled quantized contribution, so all stages operate on comparable residual scales without adding trainable parameters.",
      "specification": "For encoder output h_i and K residual codebooks, initialize r_i^(0)=h_i.       "cost_estimate": "The per-step change is K scalar divisions/multiplications on existing tensors and no additional pairwise distances or optimizer state: O(batch*d*K) elementwise work, expected well below 1% of baseline RQ-VAE step time.       "falsifiable_hypothesis": "The fixed scales make later-stage code usage and per-stage residual-energy reduction less degenerate, and this translates into higher validation and test next-item R@10 than the untempered model (targeting improvement over test_R@10 0.06335).     }
  ]
}
